objections.claim: D-006 is silent on what register status DR-115 receives on adoption and on how its condition-2 obligation is discharged, and that silence is unlawful under the regime the entry operates in. DR-115's acceptance-evidence cell is a CONJUNCTION — 'Reproducible measurements and product-owned threshold decision' — and D-006 supplies only the second conjunct. No measurement can exist yet (no harness is named, no implementation exists to measure), so DR-115 cannot become SATISFIED ('exact acceptance evidence is linked and independently reviewed') at adoption. Yet D-002 places DR-115 in the condition-2 affected-row set, which requires SATISFIED or an explicit product/architecture scope disposition before blueprint. As drafted, adoption either (a) gets misread as closing DR-115 without its acceptance evidence — the exact green-checker-elevation / promotion-by-prose class this register forbids — or (b) leaves condition 2 permanently unsatisfiable for DR-115, because reproducible measurements structurally require the implementation the blueprint gate blocks. The entry also never names the file-08 edits its commit must carry: the DR-115 row status, and the gate-registry cells that currently read 'numeric open' / 'numeric/regression open' plus the preamble sentence 'numeric pass/fail thresholds are open under DR-115', all of which become false the moment C-D006 lands and may only change through the register's own process (per D-001's turn-2 NOTE-1 discipline: checklist text and register must never disagree).

objections.claim: The DR-G03/G04 numbers are bound to 'the fixed reference runners the harness names' while ZERO harnesses are named (condition 4's harness half is measured 0/22 by D-001). Milliseconds and RSS without a named runner class are numbers with a free variable: wall-clock startup differs 3-5x between a fast developer laptop and a small CI runner, so whoever later names the G03/G04 harness silently co-authors the product threshold — a preference-laden decision escaping this entry's review. The threshold is also gameable in both directions by runner selection (choose fast hardware to pass, slow to fail). As written the falsifiability note's promise ('every number binds a HARNESS measurement') is a forward reference to an unmade, unconstrained act; the decision is not falsifiable-as-specified until that act lands, and nothing requires that act to preserve this entry's intent.
objections.evidence: docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md D-006 clause 3 ('on the fixed reference runners the harness names'); D-001 condition-4 measurement 'harness half at 0 of 22 named' (line ~124-125); register DR-G03 row harness cell 'cold-cache harness, p50/p95/p99, fixed runner image' and DR-G04 'same runners' — method described, no runner identifier named anywhere in file 08.
objections.proposedFix: Either name the reference runner class inside D-006 (e.g., a pinned CI runner image class per platform, deliberately modest, identified by name), or add a binding constraint: the G03/G04 harness-naming act is a decision commit (not gate-naming hygiene), must carry product sign-off on runner representativeness against this entry's recorded intent, and lands under D-000 review. One sentence either way; without it the ms/RSS numbers decide nothing.

objections.claim: Clause 5 and clause 6 contradict each other on adopted bytes at the second qualified release. Clause 5 decides G05 carries 'NO numeric cap' with caps deferred to first-component acceptance. Clause 6 decides 'a qualified measurement may not regress >10% against the previous qualified release' — and per-component download/install/start/RSS deltas ARE measurements published as G05 gate evidence. If they are 'qualified measurements', clause 6 imposes a de facto numeric constraint (10%-per-release growth ratchet) on exactly the quantity clause 5 says is uncapped — a hidden cap adopted while declaring none, pre-empting the deferred product decision. If they are not, clause 6's domain is undefined and component costs may regress without bound or waiver while core is ratcheted. Both readings are lawful; the ambiguity in the decided text is not, in a register whose discipline is that scope exists in bytes, never in silence.
objections.evidence: docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md D-006 clauses 5 and 6 (lines ~719-729); register DR-G05 row (evidence column 'download/install/start/RSS delta'); DR-G01/G02/G05 threshold cells say 'numeric open' while only G03/G04 say 'numeric/regression open' — the register itself does not extend a regression tolerance to G05, so clause 6's unqualified domain is D-006's own creation.
objections.proposedFix: State clause 6's domain explicitly: either 'the regression rule binds DR-G01..G04 threshold measurements only; G05 deltas are visibility-only until the deferred cap decision, which must also decide their regression tolerance' — or deliberately extend it to G05 deltas and strike the words 'NO numeric cap' in favor of 'no absolute cap; relative regression bound applies'. Either is adoptable; silence is not.

objections.claim: The G05 cap-deferral trigger — 'first-component acceptance, when a real denominator exists' — is undefined in the one place it matters: slice 1 itself ships a component. Under file 02's one-component architecture and DR-119/DR-G14, the TypeScript provider with its bundled Node closure is a signed component, and it is the slice's substrate. If it counts as the 'first component', the cap decision falls due inside slice 1 and the deferral is nearly vacuous (the denominator exists at slice-1 qualification); if it does not count, the entry never says what does — first third-party? first post-slice-1? The deferral satisfies condition 2's explicit-deferral discipline in FORM (it is recorded, not silent, and G05's claim column demands visibility rather than boundedness, so the gate remains satisfiable as specified), but its trigger cannot currently be evaluated against real events.

objections.proposedFix: Define the trigger: e.g., 'first-component acceptance = the qualification acceptance of the slice-1 TypeScript provider component; the G05 cap decision is due as a successor product decision at that acceptance, with the measured slice-1 deltas as its denominator.' If the coordinator intends a later trigger instead, name the component class that fires it.

objections.claim: Clause 6 restates the register's waiver form incompletely, and partial restatement is how rules erode. The gate-registry preamble requires FOUR properties: product and release authority, an expiry, A MEASURED RESIDUAL, and the inherited-semantic/trust-blocker exclusion. D-006's restatement — 'an expiring waiver carrying product + release sign-off (the register's waiver form)' — names two, parenthetically cites the rest, and omits the measured residual entirely. A future waiver drafted from D-006's text alone would be facially compliant with this entry and unlawful under the register. The citation does not cure it: two texts now describe one rule and the weaker one is the one adopters will read.
objections.evidence: docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md gate preamble lines 306-309 ('Waivers require product and release authority, an expiry, a measured residual, and cannot waive an inherited semantic/trust blocker') versus docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md D-006 clause 6.
objections.proposedFix: Restate the waiver form completely ('expiring waiver with product + release sign-off, a measured residual, never waiving an inherited semantic/trust blocker — the register's form, in full') or restate nothing and cite only. No third option.

objections.claim: The regression rule has no base case. 'Against the previous qualified release' is unevaluable at first qualification because zero qualified releases exist (DR-012: NOT-RELEASE-QUALIFIED, 0/25 demonstrated) — the rule's denominator is empty exactly once, at the only qualification currently in prospect. The intended semantics are obvious (rule binds from the second qualified release; the first release's retained measurements BECOME the baseline) but obvious-and-unstated is the defect class this corpus exists to kill: an adversarial reading at first qualification can claim the regression gate is unevaluable and therefore unsatisfiable, or alternatively vacuously satisfied with no baseline obligation recorded.
objections.evidence: docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md D-006 clause 6; register DR-012 row (staging record 'NOT-RELEASE-QUALIFIED (0/25 demonstrated)').
objections.proposedFix: Add the base case: 'The rule is vacuous at the first qualified release; that release's retained gate measurements are thereby designated the regression baseline, and the rule binds from the second qualified release onward.'

objections.claim: Preference honesty is uneven: clause 1 carries a rationale, clauses 2-4 carry none, and the number most in need of one — DR-G04's 100 MB RSS — fails to discriminate the precise regression the small-core architecture exists to catch: a language runtime migrating into core. File 02 defines the core by EXCLUDING language runtimes; the falsifiable-'small' purpose means each threshold should fail if that exclusion is violated. A Node-class runtime answering --version sits at roughly 40-60 MB RSS (order-of-magnitude general knowledge, flagged as such — this review cannot benchmark and the corpus records no measurements), i.e., comfortably UNDER a 100 MB bar, so the memory gate as numbered would wave through a runtime-in-core build that the download gate (25 MB vs a ~25-45 MB compressed Node closure) only marginally catches. A product owner protective of the small-core direction would plausibly choose ~50 MB for --help/--version, with doctor split out at a higher bound if probe headroom is the concern. Under D-000 the coordinator must adopt a tighter number, split the command set, or record this disagreement with the trade named.
objections.evidence: docs/v2/architecture/02-distribution-and-components.md lines 23-41 ('It excludes language runtimes, analyzers...'; ''Small' is falsifiable, not aesthetic'); D-006 clause 4 (no rationale recorded); register DR-G04 row. The Node RSS/size figures are general knowledge, explicitly NOT corpus measurements — see whatIDidNotCheck.
objections.proposedFix: Either tighten: help/version RSS peak <= 50 MB, doctor read-only <= 100 MB (recording the probe-headroom rationale); or keep 100 MB and record in the entry why the looser bar is chosen and which discrimination it deliberately gives up. Additionally add one-line rationales to clauses 2-4 matching clause 1's discipline: each number should name the regression it is sized to catch.

objections.claim: Clause 1's rationale oversells its own number. 'An order below typical Electron-class tooling' arithmetically implies ~10 MB against typical ~100 MB-class Electron compressed downloads; 25 MB is roughly 4x below, not an order. The number may be right and the prose wrong — but a rationale that flatters the number is worse than none in a register that will be audited against bytes.
objections.evidence: docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md D-006 clause 1. Electron-class figure is general knowledge, flagged as such.
objections.proposedFix: Reword to 'several-fold below typical Electron-class tooling' or tighten the number; do not adopt prose whose arithmetic fails on first inspection.

summaryForCoordinator: OBJECTIONS: 3 MUST-FIX, 4 SHOULD-FIX, 3 NOTE. The numbers themselves are mostly defensible and coherent with the small-core split (verified: they quantify over a core that excludes the TS runtime closure). The blocking defects are structural: (1) D-006 never says what DR-115 becomes on adoption while its acceptance cell conjoins measurements that cannot exist pre-blueprint — the entry must record the decided-not-measured status, the condition-2 scope disposition, and the file-08 edits its commit carries; (2) the ms/RSS thresholds bind to reference runners no harness names (0/22), leaving a 3-5x free variable to a later unreviewed act — name the runner class or bind the harness-naming act to product review of representativeness; (3) clause 5's 'NO numeric cap' for G05 contradicts clause 6's 10% regression rule at the second qualified release — state clause 6's domain. All three fixes are one-to-three sentences; none disturbs the chosen numbers except ADV-D006-07's named trade on the 100 MB RSS bar, where the coordinator must tighten, split, or record the disagreement.
